question_text: Find the number of ways of forming a committee of 5 members from 6 men and 3 ladies.

recall_prompt: Say how you would count the committees of five from six men and three ladies when there is no condition — the total to choose from, and the number.
insider_note: The split into 6 men and 3 ladies carries no condition — the committee is any 5 of the 9 people, ⁹C₅ = 126 in one line. Case work by number of ladies reaches the same 126 in four times the space.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: No condition, so choose 5 from all 9
steps.margin_note: First mark. The question puts no condition on men or ladies, so it is simply 5 people from 6 + 3 = 9: ⁹C₅.
lines: No condition on men or ladies, so choose

recall.must_convey: That with no condition the committee is any 5 of the 9 people, counted by 9 C 5.
accept: no condition so it is nine C five, five out of all nine people
add the men and ladies to nine and choose five
condition ledu kabatti nine lo five, nine C five
a committee is a selection so it is a combination of nine taken five

steps.why: The men-and-ladies split only suggests a case split; it is not needed. With no condition on the mix, every 5-person subset of the 9 is a valid committee, and a committee is a selection, so ⁹C₅.
common_mistakes: Splitting into cases by number of ladies — correct but four times the work for the same 126.
Using ⁹P₅ — a committee has no order.

steps.label: Evaluate ⁹C₅

recall.must_convey: That 9 C 5 equals 9 C 4, which is 9 times 8 times 7 times 6 over 24 = 126.
accept: nine C five is nine C four which is nine eight seven six by twenty four equals one hundred twenty six
nine C five equals one hundred and twenty six
nine C five one twenty six
three thousand twenty four by twenty four

steps.why: ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₙ₋ᵣ shortens five factors to four; the value 126 is the answer.
common_mistakes: Computing 9·8·7·6·5 = 15120 and dividing by 24 instead of 120.
